summary: Security fix: the (enterprise) agent capacity-policy user endpoints returned the full user record of other agents, including their API access token and pubsub token; they now return the public agent shape, and the shared user JSON only includes those tokens for the signed-in user themself. Capacity-policy cards fall back to the agent thumbnail for avatars.

statements.why: The commit closes a token leak (_user.json.jbuilder: access_token/pubsub_token of other users were sent via agent_capacity_policies/users index/create). Nothing new is broken, but an owner would come away thinking no security-relevant change happened, and may need to rotate tokens that were exposed.
Adds one spec file to the MFA CI run.
True but says nothing; this is where access_token/pubsub_token are now restricted to the authenticated user.
Passes the signed-in user so login responses still include their own tokens.
Now renders the agent partial instead of the full user partial.

statements.text: The agent also changed AgentCapacityPolicyCard.vue, in a way plain can't describe yet.
statements.why: Avatar falls back to user.thumbnail since the agent shape has no avatarUrl.

misses.what: This is a security fix: before it, the capacity-policy agent list/assign API returned other agents' personal API access tokens and real-time (pubsub) tokens to whoever could view the policy. Those tokens may have been exposed and could be worth rotating.
Any user response that is not about the signed-in user no longer includes access_token/pubsub_token (API clients relying on that field get nothing).
